findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, so every instance gets the same timestamp.
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` built without an explicit `queued` (including every one from `from_integration`) then carries the worker's import time, not the time it was queued. Anything that reads `queued` to order events or detect staleness gets a wrong value. Fix: `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

held.title: Task kwargs now include a raw `datetime`, which a JSON task serializer cannot encode.
held.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so the `queued` datetime object goes straight into the `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` kwargs. If the Celery task serializer is JSON (I can't see the config from here), enqueueing raises, and every inbound-triggered assignment fails to enqueue its outbound sync. If it does serialize, `from_dict` gets `queued` back as a string, and nothing checks the type. Fix: write `queued` out as an ISO string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.
